<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

ROUTE FIRST, THEN PARITY. The `pij` binary on PATH (harness/scripts/pij-cli.cjs -> .pi/extensions/pij/cli.ts) becomes generation-aware: it detects a live rs daemon and dispatches each verb to rs or legacy via an explicit ROUTE TABLE, defaulting to legacy for anything rs does not implement. That shim lands alone in wave 1, so every verb added later flips one table row and becomes reachable through the name people already type. Detection prior art exists in the pi/omp extension (.pi/extensions/pij/index.ts:283, PIJ_DAEMON_GENERATION=legacy forceback, PIJ_RS_ADDR) — reuse that mechanism, do not mint a second one. Wave 2 adds the rs verbs in usage order (PR #329's telemetry). IDENTITY IS PER-SEAT, ROUTING IS PER-VERB: once a seat registers into a generation, every identity verb for that seat resolves to the SAME generation; the fallback must never re-home a seat.

<a id="fan-out"></a>

## Fan out

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| decision | Wave 1: one unit (u-route), alone. Wave 2: three parallel units (u-report, u-identity, u-readback) against the frozen daemon HTTP contract. |
| rationale | The shim is the seam everything else arrives through, so it cannot be parallel with its consumers. Once the route table exists, verb groups are independent: they touch different HTTP handlers and different CLI subcommands, and each flips its own table rows. |

Dispatch each verb through an EXPLICIT route table — a verb is routed to rs only when listed, everything else goes legacy, so a new rs verb is a one-row change. CRITICAL DISTINCTION: rs NOT IMPLEMENTING a verb falls back; rs ERRORING does NOT fall back (masking a real failure would re-home seats silently — same family as F-1128, the two cases must be distinguishable at the call site). Provide a diagnostic that names the generation that served the last call. RULED AT THE ACK: resolve a NAMED daemon addr (two rs daemons have coexisted on this machine — a stale demo on its own state-dir), and the diagnostic prints the ADDR as well as the generation. RULED WAVE 1: the route table becomes a CAPABILITY ASK (ask rs what it serves) INTERSECTED WITH AN EXPLICIT DENY LIST — `tail` denied from day one and pinned by test even if rs advertises it. <a id="composition"></a>

## Composition

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| composer | PM, on s114/ready-on-rs. |
| steps | (1) Merge u-route first and verify the table is data-driven. (2) Merge wave-2 units, flipping one route-table row per landed verb. (3) Prove the identity-is-per-seat rule end to end: a seat registered in rs resolves ALL its identity verbs to rs, and a legacy-only seat is not silently re-homed (oq-1141's ruling governs which way it goes). (4) Live gesture: fresh Claude seat, unmodified /pij ready, lands in `pij-rs list`. |
| integration_proof | ac-1141 is the integration proof and it is an OPERATOR GESTURE, not a unit test: run the real skill in a real seat against the real rs daemon, capture the pane and the `pij-rs list` row. Plus the split-brain arm: after the gesture, `pij whoami`, `pij report now` and `pij state` for that seat all resolve to rs, proven by reading the rs store rather than by the CLI's own claim. STAGE B (o-prime owned, post-merge): canonical pulls the merge and Jordan performs the real gesture with no PATH override — recorded on req-0011, not in this PR. |

<a id="review"></a>

## Review

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| when | after composition, before the PR |
| inputs | req-0010 + req-0011 verbatim, this guide, full diff. Priority order: (1) can a seat end up half-registered across two generations, or be silently re-homed; (2) does an rs ERROR ever fall back and mask a defect; (3) does any caller asking for a transcript get the event stream; (4) do the report shapes actually match what callers type today, verified against the TS source not against the packet; (5) does a print-only adopt success exist anywhere; (6) is the route table truly data, or has per-verb logic leaked into dispatch. |
| model_override | cross-model from the coders AND from the PM (the composer is inside the blast radius — plan 111's lesson). Choose from `pij models`, filtering by the RUNTIME you are spawning, and CONFIRM THE MODEL AT THE PANE FOOTER (F-1127: a runtime-mismatched id boots a no-model seat that produces something that looks like a review). |

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| r1 | Split-brain identity: a seat live in both stores, or re-homed by a fallback — messages vanish while every surface reports success. Retired by the identity-is-per-seat rule, oq-1141's ruling, and the composition split-brain arm. |
| r2 | Fallback masks a real rs failure. Retired by the not-implemented vs errored distinction, tested both ways. |
| r3 | The `tail` false friend serves the wrong object. Retired by ac-1145 and the consumer inventory. |
| r4 | Scope creep into orchestration verbs. Retired by the non-goals: telemetry says they barely register. |
| r5 | A doc or skill edit sneaks in to make the gesture work — that would mean the routing design failed. Retired by ac-1146's mechanical zero-diff check. |
